task.description: WF-05 step 3, ARCHITECTURE-AUDITOR, dimension «architecture» of the part `team`, audit AUD-002 (run AUD-002-20261122-01). SCOPE. Architecture of Sai Team (tools/src/team and tools/src/web, 40 own files, 16353 lines): the line-by-line match of the code with decisions 0017 to 0026 (and the later records 0095, 0102, 0105 about the team core, result files and findSecrets), which AUD-001 did not check. Check: writing files all or nothing where it is promised (decisions/0004, the write phase with rename and rollback: files.js, store.js, lock.js, journal.js); protection in the same operation as the action (the lock and the journal entry are in the same operation as the change); the journal as the single source of state and the reducer that rebuilds state from it; the boundary between engine, executors, store and web (tools/src/web imports team 21 times, the team does not import web); one mechanism in all neighbouring places (AP-014: the same masking, the same path rule, the same error type in every executor and every route); dead code; files and functions too large (the engine and runner files are the likely candidates: give the lines and how the size gets in the way). EXTRA CHECKS. (1) all or nothing: the result set written by files.js (REQ-102): a failure in the middle leaves the previous state; find the test that proves it or say it is missing (2) the real executor (claude-cli.js) and the scripted executor (scripted.js) obey one interface: compare their error and stop behaviour NEEDS. The fixed copy <scratch>/aud002/tree (commit f72eaa7); read-only git (show, diff, log, grep, ls-tree against f72eaa7, e0a425b and the tags base/AUD-001-20261027-01 = b64562a and base/AUD-002-20261122-01); read-only gh; the scout's scope file for the passport of the part; the open defects in docs/issues/. NOT ALLOWED. On this PC: run npm run check, any npm script of tools/ or app/ that runs tests, node --test, the tools test scripts or the e2e tests; start Chrome; bind, probe or stop the ports 4780, 4781, 4782 and 4790; edit any project file other than your own report; commit, push, pull, checkout, stash, reset or tag. REPORT. Write your report to the file named in `output` (create the folder; JSON, 2-space indent, LF) as an object {audit:'AUD-002', part, dimension, role, subject:'f72eaa7', checked:[{check, how (the command or the files read), result}], not_checked:[{check, why}], findings:[...], summary}. A finding has the fields of WF-05 step 3: id (a short code like SEC-APP-01), check (what was checked; for requirements the requirement id and the criterion), severity (Critical, High, Medium, Low by WF-05 step 3), title, where (file and line), evidence (the command and its output, or a quote: a finding without evidence is not written), item (the bar item Q/R), recommendation (what exactly to fix and in which files). Severity by WF-05: Critical = a violation of a bar item that harms already now (a secret in files, invented events in Pixel Office, mixing of customer data, writing outside the own folder); High = a bar item not met or a criterion of a `done` requirement no longer met or a divergence from a recorded decision or a dependency with a known vulnerability; Medium = a document diverges from the files, a weak test, an outdated dependency without a known vulnerability; Low = names, dead code, formatting. Do not report a place that an open defect in docs/issues/ already covers: name the defect in `checked` instead. Do not pad: only real, evidenced findings; report what you could NOT check with the reason (this is not a finding and not a pass). In the `result` of your handoff write: verdict COMPLETED, the path of the report, the counts of findings by severity, the number of checks done and not done, and `issues` for anything ORCH or the owner must decide. The audit changes nothing in the project: your only files are the report and the result of your handoff. BE ECONOMICAL: the owner's usage limit is real. Prefer one script per group of checks, read files with targeted commands (grep, sed ranges, git show) instead of whole large files, keep narration short, and stop when the scope is covered. issues.text: ARCH-TEAM-02: is a result set meant to be all or nothing? Decision 0105 item 7 says files accepted before a refused one stay stored (scripted and claude-cli late refusal), and RB-19 proves it. If the owner wants all or nothing, that needs a new decision replacing 0105 item 7; otherwise only a test is missing for E_DISK and E_FILE_EXISTS on a later file.

Not checked (no allowed way): durability after a power loss. Result files, lock files and inbox files are linked or renamed without an fsync of the folder, while the journal event that names the file is fsynced; after a power loss the journal could name a file that is not on disk, and depsOf (runner.js 132-152) then throws E_DISK on the read. Not shown by any run; written as a doubt, not a finding.

Not measured: reducer.js reduce (line 772) clones the whole state with structuredClone at every event (Writer #prepare), so the cost of one event grows with the size of the project; no allowed command gives a real project size.

executors/proc.js stops a process group with process.kill(-pid), POSIX only. I read decision 0127 item Г ('Porting the team core to Windows is not planned') as a recorded limit and did not report it; the security report of the same part (SEC-TEAM-01) rates the same fact High on win32, so ORCH may want to settle which view stands.
Every team test cited was read, not run. For a test that runs tools/src/team/cli.js or tools/src/web/main.js (the two files that differ from main) there is no record on GitHub for the work line.
